newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- focus on supply next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- focus on supply next week.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat in typical Friday summer action, as attention turned to next week's supply.
Traders said they expected the session was basically over at noon, with prices unchanged from Thursday's level.
"People are saying, 'I'm not stretching on a Friday'," one trader said.
The Treasury market showed more vigor, with the government long bond up 8/32 at 99-17/32, pushing the yield down to 6.66 percent.

In addition to a $2.75 billion taxable pension bond deal from New Jersey next week, the tax-exempt calendar includes a $233 million sale of revenue bonds by Philadelphia International Airport through Lehman Brothers and a $220 million sale of revenues by the Delaware Valley Regional Finance, through a syndicate led by Merrill.
On the competitive side, Massachusetts planned a $300 million general obligation bond sale on June 24.

In new issue action Friday, Georgia Housing Finance Authority sold $30 million of bonds that were priced at a top yield of 5.85 percent in 2028. Senior manager Smith Barney Inc. said later in the day it had the verbal award without a change in yields.
The market next week will get several key economic reports, including durable goods for May on June 25, and the First Quarter Gross Domestic Product data on June 27.

Toward the end of the week, however, traders said activity might slow ahead of the Federal Reserve policy makers meeting, which is set for early July. While the market appeared confident that the central bank would not tighten monetary policy, it still was wary.

September muni futures rose 2/32 by midday Friday, moving to 118-13/32, while September Treasury bond futures were up 8/32 to 112-14/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 191 ticks from 197 at the close on Thursday.
In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Cleveland AMBAC 5-1/4 Certificates of Participation of 2027, which were bid at 5.53 percent, down two basis points.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2023 were bid at 5.49 percent, down one basis point.
